doc.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Life lessons: Basie's advice and Jones's ties to Sweden
summary: Baker asks about other life lessons beyond Basie's advice about the man who carried him. Jones says there are many and talks about his long friendship with the king of Sweden and feeling at home in Sweden and France.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Let me ask you something. These are life lessons when you’re talking about that. I’d really like to know, are there some other life lessons, particularly specific kinds of things? You talked once about Count Basie telling you, wait a minute. This guy carried you when you weren’t drawing all those people. Are there other life lessons . . .?
Give him half of his money back. I was in Connecticut. I’ll never forget that. He’s got a great memory.
No, you’ve got the memory, because you put a book together. Are there other life lessons that are that profound?

So many it’s unbelievable. I have been losing weight and all kinds of things lately, just because – I am lucky now – I’m fortunate that I knew [Carl XVI] Gustaf, the king of Sweden, now. I knew him way back then when we were partying with his sisters – way back in Sweden. Two of my kids have Swedish. I got a Polar Prize and all this. I feel like France and Sweden are part of my home, and the people do too. I don’t know what happened, but it’s – a skoal brother, I guess.
